audit.why: 53.93% over 777 games at 5.5/10 EVEN. Zoe owns levels 1-2 through an 800-range bubble Annie cannot answer, and Annie owns everything from 4 onward because Zoe has no real escape from her radius.

audit.why: Five of seven rows disagreed. win[] matches packet.levelChart and matches the content whys, which describe Zoe clearly winning 1-2 and Annie taking 4 onward.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings treat Portal Jump as a roaming and flanking mobility tool — 'punish her Portal Jump overextensions', 'a surprise Portal Jump sleep pick', 'caught without Portal Jump up', 'Roam early using Portal Jump's flexibility'. Sleepy Trouble Bubble's actual mechanics were never stated.
audit.why: Riot's text for Portal Jump: 'Blink to a nearby position for 1 second. Then blink back.' It is 575 range on an 11/8/5s cooldown and it returns her to where she started — it extends poke range and dodges a skillshot, but it cannot carry her anywhere, cannot escape Annie's radius, and is not a roaming tool. Sleepy Trouble Bubble meanwhile reduces the sleeping target's Magic Resist and doubles the first source of damage that breaks the sleep — that amplification, not the bubble's damage, is the kill pattern.
audit.corrected: Portal Jump described as a return-blink throughout; the MR shred and doubled waking hit written into the cooldown line and do's.
sources: brief enemyKit R and E text

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called Sleepy Trouble Bubble a fifteen-second cooldown and breakdown.cooldowns gave no number at all.
audit.why: It is 18/17/16/15/14s — 18 seconds at rank 1, and that gap is the entire green light in this lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.late says Zoe 'can still delete you from stealth'.
audit.why: Zoe has no stealth in her kit. What she has is fog-of-war and bush cover, which is a positioning problem, not invisibility — the distinction changes whether a control ward answers it.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as a bubble landed from fog.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave used the generic 'every assassin timer in the game' template.
audit.why: Zoe is not an assassin timer; her punish on a shoved wave is Paddle Star clearing from 800 while she holds the bubble for the walk-up.

edits.before: - Zoe Sleepy Trouble Bubble: matchup-defining — Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E Molten Shield has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Zoe Sleepy Trouble Bubble: 18s at rank 1 — sleep shreds your MR and doubles the first hit that wakes you, which is the Paddle Star she is saving. Body-block it with minions. - Portal Jump only blinks her back where she started: it extends her poke, it never escapes your radius.

edits.before: Sleep into empowered Q is the entire kill pattern — body-block it with minions or terrain. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Sleep shreds MR and doubles the waking hit — that is the whole kill pattern, so body-block the bubble and step up across its 18 seconds.

edits.before: Zoe burns Sleepy Trouble Bubble on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Zoe burns Sleepy Trouble Bubble on nothing — take the 18-second invitation.

edits.before: That’s Zoe’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Paddle Star gains damage the longer it flies — never eat one at max range.

edits.before: Carry through the one button — Flash-Tibbers on two is a won fight; your whole game is engineering the radius.
edits.after: Carry through one button — Portal Jump returns her to where she stood, so your radius still holds her.

edits.before: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — every assassin timer in the game points at that picture. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.
edits.after: Best wave: a Q-refund farmed wave you never push past river — your kill threat is Flash radius, not wave state. Worst wave: a shoved wave with zero stacks and Tibbers down — Zoe clears it from 800 with Paddle Star and holds the bubble for your walk-up. Crash timing: the crash is a timer you set — reset, plate, or roam, but never just because.

edits.before: Level 6: Tibbers gives you reach to punish her Portal Jump overextensions, keeping this phase in Annie's favor overall.
edits.after: Level 6: Portal Jump blinks her back where she started, so Tibbers still reaches her — the phase stays Annie's.

edits.before: Portal Jump plus a landed sleep lets Zoe delete you from near max range at level 6, but Tibbers gives you the map presence to punish her when she overextends for the kill, which is why this phase settles back to even-to-Annie.
edits.after: Portal Jump plus a landed sleep lets Zoe poke from beyond your reach at 6, but the blink returns her to where she stood, so Tibbers punishes the instant she steps up for the kill — the phase settles back to Annie.

edits.before: Level 3 onward things even out as your own stun combo starts threatening real damage, though Zoe's kit remains a coinflip since a hit sleep still swings a trade hard her way even at this stage. Once you hit level 6, Tibbers gives you the reach to punish her for overextending on Portal Jump plays, and from here the matchup tilts toward you as her one-shot potential requires a clean landed sleep while your rotation punishes any mistake she makes.
edits.after: Level 3 onward things even out as your own stun combo starts threatening real damage, though a landed sleep still swings a trade hard her way at this stage since it shreds your MR and doubles the hit that wakes you. From 6, Portal Jump blinks her back where she started rather than away, so Tibbers reaches her whenever she steps up, and the matchup tilts to you: her one-shot needs a clean bubble, your rotation needs only her mistake.

edits.before: With items in hand your stun-into-burst combo punishes her squishy HP pool severely any time she whiffs Sleep or gets caught without Portal Jump up, but never get complacent — she can still delete you from stealth with a landed bubble-into-combo, so ward and play around cooldowns rather than facechecking brush.
edits.after: With items in hand your stun-into-burst punishes her squishy HP pool any time she whiffs Sleep or steps up to poke, but never get complacent — a bubble landed out of the fog still starts a combo that deletes you, so ward and play around her 18-second cooldown rather than facechecking brush.

edits.before: Ward flanks by level 6 to avoid a surprise Portal Jump sleep pick
edits.after: Step up whenever her 18-second Sleepy Trouble Bubble is on cooldown

edits.before: Roam early using Portal Jump's flexibility while Annie lacks mobility to follow
edits.after: Roam early on side waves — Annie has no mobility at all to follow you

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged "Portal Jump's" as a probable wrong name — false positive on the name, but the surrounding claim was wrong in a worse way: six strings used Portal Jump as roaming/flanking mobility when it is a 575-range blink that returns her to her starting position. A reader acting on the old text would ward flanks against a champion that cannot flank and would decline fights she cannot actually escape. Also removed a claim that Zoe attacks 'from stealth' — she has none. Five level-chart rows disagreed between layers and were realigned to the packet chart as one group. I did not write the missing-interactions 'resistances-invalidated' line: Riot's text for Sleepy Trouble Bubble describes reduced Magic Resist and doubled waking damage, not true damage, so the trueDamage derived flag looks like a parsing misfire and I stated the real mechanic instead.
